name: Travis Tincher
position: Senior Software Engineer — Ruby on Rails · full stack · AI agents
summary: Full-stack engineer, six years in production, with Ruby on Rails and PostgreSQL at the core of the backend work and a record of shipping third-party and LLM integrations into regulated workflows. For the past year I have also built and operated an autonomous, agent-driven development system, so I know where AI tooling helps, where it lies, and how to test it.

Upgraded two consumer-facing legacy Rails applications from Ruby 2 / Rails 5 to Ruby 3 / Rails 7, adding test coverage, structured error logging, and documentation so the upgrades shipped without regressions.
Build and maintain NestJS / TypeScript services on PostgreSQL alongside the Rails work; CI/CD on GitHub Actions, AWS infrastructure via Terraform.

Built clinician-facing React / TypeScript apps for an AI smart-hospital platform (virtual nursing and observation console, admin and configuration tooling, patient-room bedside interface) deployed at NYU Langone, Johns Hopkins, Mayo Clinic and 30+ health systems.

Shipped real-time features over WebSocket and WebRTC (two-way audio/video, live sensor and location events) and surfaced AI alerts and predictions to nurses with explicit uncertainty and failure states, so a wrong signal could not pass for a right one.

Owned frontend testing and release verification (Jest, introduced Playwright end-to-end, browser validation before release, post-release checks in live hospitals); built to the design system with bedside readability and accessibility as hard requirements.

Designed and shipped an LLM document pipeline (S3 + Textract + OpenAI) that classifies and auto-sorts hundreds of scanned estate documents per client, with batching for production volume and a prompt-engineered table-of-contents output. Cut manual processing 80%, about 15 hours per client.

Moved the team from bottlenecked manual QA to a weekly release cadence behind feature flags: integrated the flag system, rebuilt the Jira automation, wrote and taught the process. Defects fell 70% and hotfixes nearly disappeared.

Built the React / TypeScript client and admin portal from scratch with a custom component library and design system; Apollo GraphQL codegen cut interface maintenance 65% and form-generator scripts cut admin form build time 90%.

Delivered a Box document-center integration in two weeks by driving the team to Box's embedded UI components; designed the executor/beneficiary permission split and the client-side Box auth flow. Added S3 versioning and admin soft-delete so the Care Team could recover any document.

Developed educational web applications for Texas elementary schools using React Native, TypeScript, and GraphQL, including interactive games to teach children about the environment and ecology, built with accessibility experts for a fully compliant UX.

experience.position: Ruby on Rails Engineer, backend lead
summary: Architected the Rails / PostgreSQL backend for a mortgage platform on AWS: ECS web and worker services, Active Job on SQS, RDS in high availability, encrypted S3 via Active Storage, Sentry and CloudWatch.

Built the Mortgage Disclosures feature end to end: Encompass and HelloSign integrations, an aasm state machine per document, webhooks for the event-driven approval flow, and Rails views for loan officers. A multi-hour manual process became a background job with two review touchpoints (~60% less manual overhead).

Designed the REST APIs serving three client portals; shipped Auth.net (payments) and PDFtron (PDF) integrations; led small projects including an external contractor; standardized inline docs with Yard and Rubocop.

experience.position: Full Stack Ruby on Rails Engineer
summary: Built the Rails API layer and page-data hydration serving the React / TypeScript client and internal Rails admin pages; shipped the digital Uniform Residential Loan Application (Form 1003) end to end; owned CI/CD in GitHub workflows and pre-launch QA.
Developed a responsive React web application for a mobile bike mechanic with Calendly scheduling and Google Maps location features.

Built and operate an autonomous development system on GitHub Issues and Projects: a queue, a runner executing one LLM session per task, a phase/wave/task hierarchy with PR-graph automation, and verification gates that decide whether agent output merges. About 3,500 tasks and 640+ merged PRs across six repos, with documented failure modes; a live multiplayer game beta shipped through it.
Earned 1st place in General Assembly’s Alumni Social Impact Hackathon.
